newsitem.title: USA: World natgas use to rise 3.1 pct annually--US EIA.
newsitem.headline: World natgas use to rise 3.1 pct annually--US EIA.

text.p: World natural gas demand should rise by 3.1 percent annually to 144.5 trillion cubic feet in 2015 from 78.3 trillion cubic feet in 1995, making it the fastest-growing fossil fuel, the U.S. Energy Information Administration said Tuesday.

Demand growth in the United States should be a smaller 1.7 percent annually and should reach 30.2 trillion cubic feet in 2015, mainly because of growth in gas-fired electricity generation, the EIA said in its annual international outlook which bases comparison on 1995 figures.

Use of natural gas in developing countries is expected to soar by 5 percent annually to reach 36.9 trillion cubic feet in 2015 from 14.0 trillion in 1995. The biggest growth is expected in China, with a 9.3 percent annual growth rate and India with an 11.1 percent annual growth rate.

The pace in industrialized countries should be a slower 2.6 percent annual increase, from 41.4 trillion cubic feet in 1995 to 68.2 trillion in 2015. That is more than twice the expected growth rate for oil in industrialized countries.
In the Former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, gas use should rise by 2.7 percent annually to 39.4 trillion cubic feet in 2015 from 23.2 trillion in 1995.
Major efforts around the world to expand gathering, transmission and distribution capabilities should allow for the demand growth, the EIA said.
